businessType: Cloud-based practice-management software for dental offices (scheduling, billing, patient records, claims). Founded 2016, 150 employees, $22M ARR, 2,500 customers, 65% gross margin.
stage: Growth: $22M ARR (+22% YoY), EBITDA margin 8% ($1.76M). Blended net revenue retention 98%, blended quarterly churn 2%. Customer concentration: top 10 customers = 35% of ARR; the single largest customer, a dental service organization (DSO) operating 300 offices, represents 12% of ARR. The independent-practice base (the other ~2,490 customers) is growing 28% YoY, while the DSO/large-group segment is growing only 5% YoY.
ownerGoal: Reach Series B readiness within 12 months with a fundable growth narrative (durable >25% ARR growth, NRR >105%, reduced single-customer concentration below 8%).
ownerConstraints: Concentration risk: top customer = 12% of ARR with annual renewal and demonstrated pricing leverage; an unfavorable renegotiation or loss creates a 12% revenue cliff.
Capital: bootstrapped-to-Series-A balance sheet; ~$6M cash, EBITDA only 8%, limited runway for large GTM bets without dilution.
Team: 150 employees with a sales motion historically optimized for large DSO deals; SMB/independent-practice motion is thinner.
Product: feature set is mature for large multi-location groups; self-serve onboarding for small practices is underdeveloped.
Time: Series B fundraising window opens in ~12 months; the growth/NRR narrative must be evidenced by then.
immediateConcern: The headline growth (22%) and acceptable blended churn (2%) mask a divergence: the small-account base is growing fast (28%) but is under-monetized (low ARPU, NRR ~99%), while the large-group segment is near-flat (5%) and concentrated. The owner wants to know where to invest the next GTM dollar to build a durable, less-concentrated growth and expansion engine before Series B.
